solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Hollywood actor can work in a creative style

parts.note: both are slang words for a toilet
art is creative work

explanation.surface: A description of a veteran film star who can still act with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning 'is able to', but it is the noun: American and British slang for a lavatory, here the British word BOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a leading star of the classic studio era, famous for Casablanca.

clue.text: Olympic officials on track for sports event

parts.note: BOA is the British Olympic Association
to track someone is to trace them

explanation.surface: Games officials stand by the running track during an athletics meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' reads as a noun for a running circuit but works as a verb, to follow or trace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest between Oxford and Cambridge universities on the Thames.

clue.text: Ring Dicky, Greek character, about my card game?

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards
dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters are in unsound order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
mu is the Greek letter M
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants to phone a dodgy Greek fellow about a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring Dicky' reads like calling a man named Dicky; in fact dicky (British for unreliable) scrambles RING into GIN R.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player variant of rummy, a card game of forming sets and runs.

clue.text: When cycling, hear South American runner

indicators.note: a cycle goes round, so the final letter comes round to the front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cyclist listens out for a South American athlete on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a flightless bird that runs rather than flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless bird of the South American grasslands, built for fast running like the ostrich.

clue.text: Blog Joe broadcast before noon entering mountain range

indicators.note: placed first in the line, so one piece precedes the rest
to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the Urals divide Europe from Asia
N is a standard abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A blogger named Joe posts a morning update from the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The noon letter goes inside the mountain range, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is an online diary, and a journal published electronically is that kind of record.

clue.text: Private room, with Elizabeth meeting Jeremy, an author of poems

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a private room
Bet is a short form of Elizabeth
Jem is a pet form of Jeremy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet holds a private meeting with two people, Elizabeth and Jeremy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' looks like part of the definition 'an author of poems' but also serves as the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Betjeman was a much-loved English poet and Poet Laureate from 1972 to 1984.

clue.text: Part of body captured by Paul Nash

indicators.note: what is captured is held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: A painter's portrait of a part of the human figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Nash was an English landscape painter, so 'captured by' reads like something painted by him.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Hold salt over vessel
Hide mattress in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a Lilo is a British brand of inflatable air mattress used at the beach or pool

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a mattress inside a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lilo is the British name for an inflatable airbed; said out loud it matches the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for keeping out of sight and avoiding attention, which is hiding.

clue.text: Stoppage of breathing happens one day, occasionally

indicators.note: now and then rather than always, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A medical note that a patient now and then stops breathing during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on. APNOEA is the British spelling; Americans write apnea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apnoea is the medical term for a temporary suspension of breathing, as in sleep apnoea.

clue.text: Fabric woman laid up in church

indicators.note: to be in something is to be enclosed by it, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
hen is informal for a woman, as in a hen party
someone laid up is confined to bed, unwell

explanation.surface: A woman lies ill in church, perhaps wrapped in some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' looks like a reversal signal but simply means bedridden. A hen night is a British bride's party before her wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a tufted, velvety yarn or cloth, used for bedspreads and soft furnishings.

clue.text: Big cheese, four ounces, on small base

parts.note: a big cheese is the boss, the head
four ounces is a quarter of a pound
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a lump of cheese weighing four ounces at the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big cheese' looks like part of a shopping list; it is slang for an important person. A quarter is a quarter-pound in imperial weights.
explanation.definitionFit: Headquarters is the central office or operational base from which an organisation or army is run.

clue.text: Republican getting unpopular after severe defeat

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for Republican
out of favour, no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A Republican politician loses support after a crushing election loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks as though it orders the pieces, but it belongs to the definition-side surface; the letters simply run in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a decisive, overwhelming loss in which the beaten side is scattered.

clue.text: Classic porcelain

definitions.meaning: one of the five English Classic horse races, run at Epsom each June
fine bone china named after the Midlands city where it is made

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic porcelain' reads as one phrase for antique china. In British racing the Classics are five major flat races for three-year-olds.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a famous Epsom horse race and the bone china produced in that Midlands city.

clue.text: Goon in New York, over with sketch writer

parts.note: Boz was Dickens's pen name in Sketches by Boz
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A comedy writer in New York works with a clownish character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In New York' marks the definition as American slang. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bozo is American slang for a foolish or oafish person, much like the British goon.

clue.text: Update of Hound Dog, say, fast track covered by the King

indicators.note: something covered is wrapped up inside another thing

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
the M1 is Britain's first long motorway, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Elvis, the King, records a fast new version of Hound Dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King' points to Elvis, but it is the Latin word for king. The M1 is a motorway running north from London.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a reworked version of a recorded song, and Hound Dog is an example of a track.

clue.text: Bent Asian money disheartened Kathy

parts.note: the won is the currency of both Koreas

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the centre, so only the ends remain

parts.note: the name without its middle letters

explanation.surface: A dishonest Asian fortune leaves poor Kathy dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' suggests corrupt money, but here it means crooked in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonky is informal British for askew or crooked, not straight, which is what bent describes.

clue.text: Remark about lawyer, one earning praise

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a remark is a comment
DA is an American district attorney
the Roman numeral for one
what you are on is what you earn, as in on a good salary

explanation.surface: A comment about a lawyer who is winning plaudits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One earning praise' reads as a person, but splits into two short pieces before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A commendation is a formal expression of approval or an official award recognising merit.

clue.text: Visiting fanatic up in Greenland's capital, acclimatising

parts.note: visiting a place is being at it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital is the leading letter of a word, so only the first is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A zealot on a visit to Nuuk gets used to the Arctic cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenland's capital' wants to be Nuuk; in crosswords a capital is often just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Attuning is adjusting or bringing into harmony with surroundings, as acclimatising does with a climate.

clue.text: Winner from Belize, half grabbed by press agent

indicators.note: what is grabbed is held inside another's grip

parts.note: a PR man handles public relations for a client

indicators.note: half a word keeps only one of its two equal parts

parts.note: the back three of its six letters

explanation.surface: A publicist snatches a champion visiting from Belize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winner from Belize' reads as one phrase, but 'from Belize' belongs to the wordplay. A PR man is a public-relations agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A prizeman is someone who has won a prize, especially an academic award at a university.

clue.text: Reckon fish right for winter sportsperson?

parts.note: to figure is to reckon or calculate
the skate is a flat sea fish
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An angler thinks a fish is just the thing for a winter athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a figure skater is one kind of winter sportsperson.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure skating is an Olympic ice sport performed in the Winter Games, so its competitors are winter athletes.

clue.text: It's on the agenda to cut most of little tree

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one piece is set inside the other
most but not all means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a baby is a little one
AOB, any other business, is the last item on a meeting's agenda

explanation.surface: A meeting's agenda includes pruning a small tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' is used as a noun, a little one. AOB, any other business, closes most British meeting agendas.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a massive-trunked African tree, sometimes called the upside-down tree.

clue.text: Ruffian's long time encased by some thermal insulation

indicators.note: something encased is surrounded on all sides by an outer layer

parts.note: the tog is a unit measuring the warmth of a duvet
an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: A thug spends a long stretch wrapped in insulating material.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a contraction of 'is', linking definition to wordplay. Duvets in Britain are rated in togs.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang for a scoundrel or petty villain, a contemptible rough type.

clue.text: American car recruits love to maintain

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: to recruit is to take someone in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: VW is a Volkswagen
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A US car maker hires staff who love keeping vehicles in good repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maintain' suggests servicing a car; here it means to assert something firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or affirm openly, just as one maintains a claim is true.

clue.text: Feeble limiting radius needs exercise

indicators.note: a limit forms a boundary, so the outer word bounds the inner one

parts.note: feeble and weak are synonyms
r is the symbol for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A frail patient with a restricted range of movement needs a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' reads as a noun for physical training; it is the verb, as in exercising power.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreak vengeance or havoc is to inflict or exert it, the sense of exercising influence.

clue.text: Grill squid, edging removed by unknown

indicators.note: taking off the border leaves just the inside of the word

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters
z is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A cook barbecues squid after trimming its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' is cooking in the surface but means interrogate. Mathematicians label unknowns x, y and z.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiz someone is to question them closely, which is what grilling a suspect means.

clue.text: Seconds of TV dinner — and booze such as this?

definitions.text: Seconds of TV dinner — and booze such as this?

indicators.note: the second item in each word, so the letter in position two is kept each time

parts.note: second letter
second letter
second letter
second letter

explanation.surface: A TV supper with second helpings, washed down with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like extra servings of food; it means second letters. The whole clue also describes what you might drink with that meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vino is informal for wine, the kind of booze served alongside a dinner in front of the television.

clue.text: Fine loose linen shirt sourced here?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
lax and loose both mean slack

explanation.surface: A fine, loose-fitting linen shirt, and where it comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by description, hence the question mark: the plant is where linen comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is woven from the fibres of the flax plant, so a linen garment originates in it.

clue.text: Maybe Dietrich's key part of script involved in sin

parts.note: B is a musical key

indicators.note: something involved in another is caught up inside it

parts.note: to err is to do wrong, to sin
an actor learns lines from a script

explanation.surface: Marlene Dietrich's crucial line in a film script involves something sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks Dietrich as an example; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was born in Berlin, so she is an example of a native of that German city.

clue.text: Pan one initially used, mixing onions, garlic etc

parts.note: pan- is the Greek-derived prefix meaning all
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: what comes initially comes at the start, so the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A cook uses one frying pan to combine onions and garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' reads as a cooking pot and 'mixing' as an anagram signal; both mislead. Pan means all, as in pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Allium is the botanical genus containing onions, garlic, leeks, chives and shallots.

clue.text: Villa perhaps given penalty

definitions.meaning: a villa is an example of a large dwelling

definitions.note: a place, where one goes when given a penalty
definitions.meaning: slang for prison, where a convicted person is sent

explanation.surface: Aston Villa, a football team, is awarded a penalty kick.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa is an English football club, so 'Villa ... given penalty' sounds like a match report.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large residence; the big house is American slang for a prison, the result of a sentence.

clue.text: Element of info on beef curry at the back

indicators.note: placed on top of in a written line means coming after

parts.note: beef comes from the ox

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Nutritional details on a beef curry printed on the packet's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' looks like 'part of', the start of a phrase; it is the definition, a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxygen is the chemical element with atomic number eight, essential for respiration.
